titleStmt.title: Visualization of Categorization: How to See the Wood and the Trees
titleStmt.author: Ophir Münz-Manor
Itay Marienberg-Milikowsky

bibl.title: Visualization of Categorization: How to See the Wood and the Trees

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: Figurative language in a corpus of late-antique Hebrew liturgical poetry, investigated from both a manual and a computational point of view.
span.quote: we present, theorize and contextualize an investigation of figurative language in a corpus of Hebrew liturgical poetry from late antiquity, from both a manual and a computational point of view.

span.label: How much room is there for sample-based research in a computationally-based annotation process, and can a particular concept of categorization support it?
span.quote: How much room is there for sample-based research in a computationally-based annotation process? Could a particular concept of categorization support it?

span.label: Proposes a playful approach to the epistemological status of categories, in which they are returned to and re-examined critically rather than fixed at the start of annotation.
span.quote: we propose a more playful approach to the epistemological status of categories, one that does not leave them solely as the cornerstone of the annotation process, but returns to examine them again and again from a critical perspective.

span.label: method
span.quote: in what follows we introduce a tool that is designed, among other things, to enable just that: at one and the same time to take advantage of categorization while also fostering speculation.

span.label: a hermeneutical circle in which visualizing the annotations sends the analyst back to re-assess the categories that produced them
span.quote: after visualizing the material in this way, it often turns out that the categories themselves need to be re-assessed. In other words, the categorization and visualization in themselves create a sort of hermeneutical circle in which both parts influence one another reciprocally.

span.label: case study
span.quote: Through the case study, we seek to demonstrate that, by using correct methods and tools (not only ViS-À-ViS but others also), one can ultimately use visualization of categorization as the basis for what might be called

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the original annotations are carried into the digital tool untouched, a rule the authors adopt because whether a word is figurative is a hermeneutical decision that differs between annotators and within one annotator at a later date
span.quote: Here we took another important decision, which was to stick strictly to the original annotations in order for the experiment to be as sound as possible. As literary scholars, who cannot ignore the subjective nature of interpretation, it was an intuitive act: the decision whether a word is figurative or not is a hermeneutical one, and different scholars would tend to annotate the word differently. Moreover, even the same annotator might interpret the word differently at a later date or in a different context. It was because of this that we decided not to touch the original annotations when migrating from the analogue dissertation to the digital experiment; but we shall return to this point towards the end of this article.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the corpus's figurative share is correlated against two further corpora newly annotated for figurative language - the Psalms and a ninth-century poet - which is what supplies an answer to the question the dissertation could not answer, small in comparison to what
span.quote: But “small” in comparison to what? In the dissertation this question could not have been answered and probably did not seem worthwhile at the time. In order to correlate the results, we examined them against two new corpora that have now been annotated for figurative language: the Book of Psalms from the Bible and the poetry of Pinchas the Priest, a ninth-century poet from Tiberias.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: a per-genre ratio of figurative to non-figurative words, set against the corpus-wide rate, which is what converts a qualitative impression about a genre into a checkable quantity
span.quote: The quantification of the results allowed one to examine easily what the figurative density (the ratio between figurative and non-figurative words) of each genre might be, and here, too, the results corroborated some of the initial findings while refuting others. Most notably is the genre of the Hosha’not (hosanna), which ranked at 25% of figurative density. That is to say, in general, every fourth word is figurative. If we compare this phenomenon to the overall figurative density of the corpus, which is 11%, it really stands out.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: annotation counts are aggregated into ten-percent chunks of each text, which normalises length and is what makes a positional pattern comparable across poems of different sizes
span.quote: The figures below visualize the annotations’ distribution in four Avodah poems. The left-hand side represents the beginning of the text, and the right-hand side its end. The vertical axis represents the number of figurative usages, aggregated per ten-percent chunks of the texts

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: individual tags can be withdrawn from the chart as well as added, so a pattern is exposed by subtracting annotations rather than only by displaying them
span.quote: What is more, this visualization is interactive, and with a single click a tag can be added or withdrawn from the screen, thus enabling the user to play with the visualization and consider different views and interpretation modes. Here, one of the core features of the tool comes into play, one that gives it its experimental nature, namely, the ability not only to visualize the annotations statically but also to add or eliminate some of them in order to reveal different aspects of the texts and the patterns embedded within them.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: a tagset too large and too hierarchical to grasp in the annotation tool itself is given an interactive network-oriented representation in the separate visualisation tool
span.quote: Large, hierarchical tagsets are hard to grasp and visualize in CATMA, and ViS-À-ViS offers an interactive representation of the tagset in a network-oriented chart

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the chart collapses and uncollapses level by level, and a level's size is drawn as the number of children it has, which is what makes the inner hierarchy of the tagset readable as shape
span.quote: Here a representation of the tagset is visible and the interactive chart enables one to collapse or uncollapse the various levels. The size of each level relates to the number of children it has, which once more offers a useful insight into the structure and inner hierarchy of the tagset.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the annotations of two or more annotators are viewed side by side, which is what turns the scholar's attention to the individual and subjective interpretation of each annotator instead of to a single reading of the text
span.quote: As was previously noted, CATMA, and thus also ViS-À-ViS, support multiple annotations and annotators. This way the user can view side-by-side the annotations of two or more annotators in order to compare and analyze them. This turns the attention of the scholar to the individual and subjective interpretation of each annotator and presents therefore another insight into potential patterns in the text. This in turn provides additional evidence for the corroboration or refutation of scholarly hypotheses about the text and about the differences and similarities between the different annotators

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the variation between annotators is not collapsed into a gold or a silver standard; the multiplicity is visualised instead, so the disagreement is left as a question about the correct annotation rather than answered
span.quote: Instead of collapsing the variation into a gold or a silver standard, ViS-À-ViS advocates for the visualization of multiplicity. In other words, instead of providing an answer concerning the “correct” annotation, it raises a question about it and promotes once more literary speculation.

span.label: Annotation is stated to be hermeneutical and unstable across annotators and across time, including within the same annotator.
span.quote: the decision whether a word is figurative or not is a hermeneutical one, and different scholars would tend to annotate the word differently. Moreover, even the same annotator might interpret the word differently at a later date or in a different context.

span.label: The original annotation phase had no well-defined tagset and the category definitions were flexible.
span.quote: In hindsight, although there existed a notion of a clear-cut categorization of figurative language in the corpus, no well-defined tagset was created.

span.label: The examples analysed in the original work were not selected for representativity.
span.quote: these examples weren’t chosen for their representativity, but because they were interesting or important to the author for some reason or other.

span.label: Moving from many annotated texts to a statement about the corpus is said to involve an almost inevitable reduction.
span.quote: even if we find the most creative ways to build a database of texts that classifies them on the basis of a complicated calculation of all their annotations and internal relationships, in the end, some degree of reduction is almost inevitable.

span.label: The paper states that adopting the computational option carries a price rather than delivering objectivity.
span.quote: the transition to a digital tool might well have coincided with a certain and widespread perception of the adopting of the computational option as a move in the direction of objectivity, scientification, and the like. However, as we shall see, and as other scholars have already argued, the picture is more complex, since, even in such a case, this move has a price

span.label: The paper argues that excessive textual anchoring of speculation and hypothesis carries a cost.
span.quote: We argue that excessive textual anchoring of speculations and hypotheses comes with a price, and offer a visualization approach that tries to deal with this

span.label: The exploratory visualization phase is declared unpredictable in duration and in whether it yields anything.
span.quote: it is very difficult to frame exactly this exploratory phase, to predict how long will it take or to predict its fruitfulness.

span.label: The tool interoperates with one annotation system only.
span.quote: At the moment it works exclusively with CATMA.

span.label: A quantitative and a qualitative reading of the same genre disagree, and the paper holds both to be valid rather than resolving them.
span.quote: Here we encounter an interesting case where the quantitative and the qualitative represent separate lines that do not meet while both are valid.

span.label: The price of a category system is named as an effect on the annotator, not on the data: students become addicted to it and are described as ending in a different intellectual position from the one they started in.
span.quote: Once they are exposed to the power of systematic annotation, they become addicted to it. They fall in love with the straight-forward use of a category system: it offers them an attractive intellectual alternative in its solidity, in its precision, in its caution. They start like Culler, and end like Piper.

span.label: The stated end state of the process is that the interpretation itself becomes rigid.
span.quote: they transform their annotations into something tangible, and the process comes to a head: metadata becomes data, and interpretation becomes a rigid text.

span.label: A claim in the author's own earlier dissertation is identified as incorrect by the quantitative measure, and the paper says so in print, naming the source: the genre was described as low on figurative language and measures at more than twice the corpus density.
span.quote: Curiously, in Münz-Manor’s dissertation it was noted, in passing to be honest, that this genre is low on figurative language [ Münz-Manor 2006a , p. 61]. Where did such an incorrect assertion come from?

span.label: The reason the human reading was wrong is named, and it is not carelessness: the words are figurative but the poem does not sound figurative, so impression and count come apart.
span.quote: The Hosha’not are very short and in the style of a litany, a list of attributes of the people of Israel. So even if many of these epithets are figurative, the poem as a whole does not sound very figurative.

span.label: annotation
span.quote: human digital annotation is based on sensitive attention to every detail in the text, and is definitely a way of reading.

span.label: tagset
span.quote: the notion of a tagset as a defined and more or less stable logical representation of the categories was not an idea Münz-Manor had thought of.

span.label: modeling
span.quote: This problem, in brief, stems from the multifaceted nature of digital modeling operations – including annotating, as a form of modeling

span.label: in-line annotation
span.quote: We suggest the term in-line annotation to refer to the practice of annotating specific aspects in a text, rather than producing a label for the text as a whole.

span.label: inter-annotator agreement
span.quote: Inter-annotator agreement (or lack thereof) is a fundamental term in computational linguistics and natural language processing, fields that seek to minimize human variation and to create standards

span.label: visualization of multiplicity
span.quote: Instead of collapsing the variation into a gold or a silver standard, ViS-À-ViS advocates for the visualization of multiplicity.

span.label: close reading
span.quote: unlike close reading, where the scholar actually reads the text closely, distant reading – regardless of its specific history [ Ross 2014 ] [ Herrnstein-Smith 2016 ] [ Underwood 2017 ] – is better understood as a metaphor

span.label: distant reading
span.quote: the reader extracts meaning from the corpus without actually reading it, à la Moretti. Analyzing text via visualization, then, is a perfect example of “reading” a text, without reading it at all.

span.label: text classification
span.quote: text classification – and genre classification is a good example of this – is a device designed to connect their parts together

span.label: CATMA
span.quote: CATMA is a powerful and flexible tool that focuses on annotation, hence its visualization capabilities are basic.

span.label: ViS-À-ViS
span.quote: This reality was the incentive for the creation of a separate tool, ViS-À-ViS , that enables the user to visualize the annotated text, the annotations (by one or more annotators) and even the tagset itself

span.label: category system
span.quote: They fall in love with the straight-forward use of a category system: it offers them an attractive intellectual alternative in its solidity, in its precision, in its caution.

span.label: systematic annotation
span.quote: Once they are exposed to the power of systematic annotation, they become addicted to it.

span.label: figurative density
span.quote: The quantification of the results allowed one to examine easily what the figurative density (the ratio between figurative and non-figurative words) of each genre might be, and here, too, the results corroborated some of the initial findings while refuting others.

span.label: Hosha’not
span.quote: Most notably is the genre of the Hosha’not (hosanna), which ranked at 25% of figurative density.

span.label: categorization - built upward from the data, by collecting instances until a category that contains them is defined
span.quote: a categorization based on generalizations – that is, collecting and extracting all the data until categories that contain them correctly are defined

span.label: categorization - built downward by formalization, by removing actual data until an abstract category remains
span.quote: versus a categorization based on formalization, that is, by removing all actual data until an abstract category is formed

span.label: reading - distant reading, which the paper says is better understood as a metaphor, since meaning is extracted without reading the text
span.quote: distant reading – regardless of its specific history [ Ross 2014 ] [ Herrnstein-Smith 2016 ] [ Underwood 2017 ] – is better understood as a metaphor. In other words, the reader extracts meaning from the corpus without actually reading it

span.label: annotation - a close reading practice, based on sensitive attention to every detail in the text
span.quote: human digital annotation is based on sensitive attention to every detail in the text, and is definitely a way of reading.

span.label: annotation - a modelling operation that prepares the object for future, as-yet-unknown questions
span.quote: such operations sometimes seek to focus on a specific pre-defined research question, at the same time as seeking to prepare the research object for future analysis, based on as-yet-unknown questions

span.label: inter-annotator variation - the driving force of interpretation, to be visualized rather than collapsed into a standard
span.quote: Instead of collapsing the variation into a gold or a silver standard, ViS-À-ViS advocates for the visualization of multiplicity.

span.label: the price of a category system - not inaccuracy but ATTRACTION: solidity, precision and caution are named as what makes it seductive, and the seduction is the cost
span.quote: They fall in love with the straight-forward use of a category system: it offers them an attractive intellectual alternative in its solidity, in its precision, in its caution.

span.label: figurative density - a counted ratio of figurative to non-figurative words, which for one genre is 25% against a corpus figure of 11%
span.quote: The quantification of the results allowed one to examine easily what the figurative density (the ratio between figurative and non-figurative words) of each genre might be, and here, too, the results corroborated some of the initial findings while refuting others. Most notably is the genre of the Hosha’not (hosanna), which ranked at 25% of figurative density. That is to say, in general, every fourth word is figurative. If we compare this phenomenon to the overall figurative density of the corpus, which is 11%, it really stands out.

span.label: figurative density - the aesthetic impression of figurativeness, which the paper states can be LOW in the same poem whose counted density is high
span.quote: Quantitatively, there are many figurative words, however, their aesthetic impression is low and possibly does not call for a detailed literary analysis; or does it?

span.label: distinguishes-from → Franco Moretti, distant reading
span.note: differs in: WHETHER EACH TEXT IS INTERPRETED ON THE WAY. The method reaches the same place - a claim about a whole corpus - and the paper refuses the label anyway: 'this is NOT another version of Franco Moretti's distant reading, because, UNLIKE MORETTI, WHEN WE SERIOUSLY ANNOTATE TEXT AFTER TEXT WE DO INTERPRET IT.' The distinction is in the procedure, not in the output, which is why it is invisible in the result
span.quote: To be clear, this is not another version of Franco Moretti’s distant reading, because, unlike Moretti, when we seriously annotate text after text we do interpret it.

span.label: builds-on → Rieder and Röhle (2012)
span.note: differs in: WHETHER GOING COMPUTATIONAL BUYS OBJECTIVITY. The move is described as widely PERCEIVED as 'a move in the direction of objectivity, scientification, and the like', and then: 'HOWEVER, as we shall see, and as other scholars have already argued, THE PICTURE IS MORE COMPLEX, since, even in such a case, THIS MOVE HAS A PRICE'. The borrowed claim is that a method change costs something rather than only adding rigour
span.quote: the transition to a digital tool might well have coincided with a certain and widespread perception of the adopting of the computational option as a move in the direction of objectivity, scientification, and the like. However, as we shall see, and as other scholars have already argued, the picture is more complex, since, even in such a case, this move has a price [ Rieder and Röhle

span.label: qualifies → Piper
span.note: differs in: WHICH COMPUTATIONAL PRACTICE THE ARGUMENT IS PAIRED WITH. The agreement is stated first - 'Our approach here is NOT VERY DIFFERENT FROM PIPER'S' - and the difference is the instrument: projects relying on 'the SYSTEMATIC ANNOTATION OF TEXTS, RATHER THAN ON MACHINE LEARNING ALGORITHMS, which - despite being based on pre-existing annotated texts - EMPHASIZE THE DISTANCE FROM THE TEXT ITSELF'. Same argument, different tooling, and the reason given is proximity to the text
span.quote: Our approach here is not very different from Piper’s, although we believe that this argument goes quite naturally hand in hand with computational research projects that rely heavily on the systematic annotation of texts, rather than on machine learning algorithms, which – despite being based on pre-existing annotated texts – emphasize the distance from the text itself.

span.label: extends → Marienberg-Milikowsky et al. (2022)
span.note: differs in: WHAT TO DO WITH DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN ANNOTATORS. The prior work argued variation is the driving force of interpretation; this paper turns that into a tool behaviour: 'INSTEAD OF COLLAPSING THE VARIATION INTO A GOLD OR A SILVER STANDARD, ViS-À-ViS advocates for the VISUALIZATION OF MULTIPLICITY ... instead of providing an answer concerning the "correct" annotation, it RAISES A QUESTION about it'. Inter-annotator disagreement stops being noise to be resolved and becomes the displayed result
span.quote: Instead of collapsing the variation into a gold or a silver standard, ViS-À-ViS advocates for the visualization of multiplicity. In other words, instead of providing an answer concerning the “correct” annotation, it raises a question about it and promotes once more literary speculation

span.label: annotation —is-a→ modeling
span.quote: This problem, in brief, stems from the multifaceted nature of digital modeling operations – including annotating, as a form of modeling

span.label: in-line annotation —distinct-from→ text classification
span.quote: Text annotation is a device designed to break down texts; text classification – and genre classification is a good example of this – is a device designed to connect their parts together, in order to achieve at least one generalization regarding the text

span.label: inter-annotator agreement —contrasted-with→ visualization of multiplicity
span.quote: Inter-annotator agreement (or lack thereof) is a fundamental term in computational linguistics and natural language processing, fields that seek to minimize human variation and to create standards [ Plank 2022 ]. In “traditional” literary studies variation is frequently the driving force of the hermeneutical process – and, as we argued elsewhere, we think it can and should be the same in the field of computational literary studies [ Marienberg-Milikowsky et al. 2022 ]. Instead of collapsing the variation into a gold or a silver standard, ViS-À-ViS advocates for the visualization of multiplicity.

span.label: ViS-À-ViS —distinct-from→ CATMA
span.quote: This reality was the incentive for the creation of a separate tool, ViS-À-ViS , that enables the user to visualize the annotated text, the annotations (by one or more annotators) and even the tagset itself

span.label: close reading —contrasted-with→ distant reading
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS WHETHER THE TEXT IS ACTUALLY READ. 'UNLIKE CLOSE READING, WHERE THE SCHOLAR ACTUALLY READS THE TEXT CLOSELY, distant reading - regardless of its specific history - is BETTER UNDERSTOOD AS A METAPHOR.' The contrast is not two techniques on a scale of distance; one names an activity and the other is said to name none. Q-463. · strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: unlike close reading, where the scholar actually reads the text closely, distant reading – regardless of its specific history [ Ross 2014 ] [ Herrnstein-Smith 2016 ] [ Underwood 2017 ] – is better understood as a metaphor

span.label: Visualising the annotations repeatedly forced the categories to be revised.
span.quote: after visualizing the material in this way, it often turns out that the categories themselves need to be re-assessed

span.label: Categorisation and visualisation form a hermeneutic circle: each changes the other.
span.quote: the categorization and visualization in themselves create a sort of hermeneutical circle in which both parts influence one another reciprocally

span.label: The first annotation pass had a working notion of categories but no defined tagset — the tagset came later.
span.quote: although there existed a notion of a clear-cut categorization of figurative language in the corpus, no well-defined tagset was created

span.label: The initial scheme was flat: four devices with no hierarchy between them.
span.quote: The major figurative devices were annotated in an entirely flat hierarchy of metaphor, metonymy, synecdoche and simile.

span.label: 25% — figurative density of the Hosha'not genre: one word in four
span.quote: Most notably is the genre of the Hosha’not (hosanna), which ranked at 25% of figurative density. That is to say, in general, every fourth word is figurative.

span.label: 11% — figurative density of the whole corpus, the comparison the 25% stands out against
span.quote: If we compare this phenomenon to the overall figurative density of the corpus, which is 11%, it really stands out.
